answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to earn and cheap to verify: every new identity starts at the nadir of trust and must build standing through attested, useful work over time, with a small stake locked behind it. Spawning a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand times the work and stake, while one honest agent climbs steadily. Like a falcon proving its hunting skill before flying with the flock, privileges scale with a proven record, not a claimed name. Each identity is like an opal: its value lies in a unique, costly history that cannot be cheaply copied.
